@sunnyhaibin I happened to have a weird occurrence today (also it being the first day of me using C3X with sunnypilot and CHLR). I was driving at night and it was drizzling heavily, but CHLR was doing great for the most part. I had stopped at a red light and reactivated smart cruise control  on green. Speed limit was set to 45 and there were other red lights coming up. Next light was maybe 1000ish meters away. Car accelerated to 45 and steady, but there was another car waiting at the next red light in my lane. I was assuming it would start slowing down, but it showed no signs of doing so. I had to brake quite close and heavily in the end to get it to stop behind the other car. I had not yet figured out how to get it to stop for red lights and stop signs, but I expected it to slow down and come to a stop for the car in front. Am I doing something wrong, or was this genuinely unexpected behavior?

it doesn’t sound like you have enabled openpilot longitudinal control and experimental mode, and even if you had, red lights are not expected to work fully and are still in early development. right now im guessing you’re still using the cars stock longitudinal (gas and brake) control, which means openpilot is only controlling steering and can do nothing about slowing and speeding the car

@0ppast0ppa I said weird occurence because it was just that one time. Longitudinal control appears to be working since it drove (acclerated and braked) behind other cars in traffic automatically. There were no issues at that time. As for the red lights and stop signs, I am not sure if there is something to enable them, or they just work out of the box, because it has never slowed down for a stop sign. I am going to check my settings again, but I am pretty sure about the longitudinal control working fine, rather working. 🙂

Yeah stock longitudinal control accelerates and brakes for lead cars (usually brakes extremely late for stopped cars as you described due to radar limitations), what I’m talking about is openpilot longitudinal control. that’s different, because enabling that is what disables the system that already came with your car with another system that’s run on the comma device. when the comma device is the one controlling gas and brakes, you can enable experimental mode and it will (try to) stop for lights and signs. one way to tell you’re on experimental mode is it won’t accelerate to and hold set speeds as you described, it usually drives slow and does not hold set speeds

@0ppast0ppa Ah, that makes a lot more sense, but I have run into a problem. I tried what you said and it is causing an error. First up, I am running dev-c3 on a C3X on a 2024 Ioniq 5 Limited. When I enable OpenPilot longitudinal control and experimental mode, it throws up an EPB error on the dash cluster (I suspect a forward collision avoidance system error) as soon as C3X finishes booting up. I am not able to enable ACC at all when this happens. When I press the LCA button on my steering wheel, I think it turns on the stock LCA as the icon for it is the steering wheel symbol in the center. When C3X controls both, I never see that icon and it is just the LKAS icon active which does both LKAS and LCA. The EPB error goes away when I turn off OpenPilot longitudinal control and experimental mode and it works as intended, albeit without the features we are discussing.

@0ppast0ppa One thing I would like to verify is that there are two settings in the "Toggles" menu. One says OpenPilot Longitudinal Control and the other is Custom Stock Longitudinal Control. Which one are you referring to here? I ask because enabling the former results in the error I mentioned above, and the latter does not. I am going to try driving it with the second one and see what happens.

im talking about the first, custom stock does not stop for lights and such but is better than the OEM system because it does a better job of slowing for turns and adapting to speed limits by simulating manual button presses on your stock system. unfortunately i cannot help with the technical questions, hopefully one of the devs can help you out @DevTekVE @sunnyhaibin
@0ppast0ppa Thank you. I am going to post pictures here in a bit, since enabling the first one causes the error, but the second one does not.
Case 1: OpenPilot LC enabled, EBP, Forward Collision System Error
Case 2: Same error even with Experimental Mode toggled off
Case 3: Custom Stock LC enabled does not result in any error and works fine.
